Sensor case and car mount

Handheld case. Three printed parts: the front shell, the battery side, and a car adapter that zip-ties to a wing mirror. The case stands on its switch edge in the adapter, sensors facing sideways.

Parts

    0 mm
    off

    Slide left to slice across the case and see the two flanges on its switch edge, and the adapter's head held between them.

    How it goes together

    1. Board into the front shell. Component side down, sensor cans through the collars and the air blade through its slot, two M2 × 5 screws into the bosses.
    2. Cell into the battery side. It slides into the open end like a drawer; the lead comes up past the end of the board to the JST.
    3. Battery side onto the front shell. Four M2 × 8 screws. The shell's skirt closes the open end, so the cell is held.
    4. Adapter onto the mirror. Two 5 mm zip ties, one through each tunnel in its plate and round the mirror housing. Foam tape behind it if the mirror is curved.
    5. Case onto the adapter. On its switch edge, lanyard end first, so the adapter's head slides into the channel between the case's two flanges, until the case meets the stop and the arm clicks into its notch. Press the arm's tab away from the case to release.
